rationale: The ticket fixes the migration bootstrap: ApplyBaselineAsync currently inserts every known migration into __EFMigrationsHistory before MigrateAsync, so a pre-migration database that already has ScrapeJobs/ScrapeRuns/Listings reports itself up to date while missing all later schema. The contract is test-only and declares no new production surface: it drives the existing public ApplyMigrations extension and observes database state. LegacyDatabaseMigrationAddsStatusChangeTableTests builds a database at 20260911124753_InitialCreate with IMigrator, drops __EFMigrationsHistory to reproduce the reported pre-migration database, applies migrations, and asserts the ListingStatusChanges table plus the later Listings columns now exist (AC-1). LegacyDatabaseMigrationPreservesListingRowsAndValuesTests seeds a ScrapeJob/ScrapeRun/Listing in that legacy database, applies migrations, reads the rows back through the EF model, and asserts the seeded values survive while later columns stay null (AC-2). AC-3 reuses the existing MigrationsLeaveUpToDateDatabaseUnchangedTests and AC-4 reuses MigratedListingSchemaIncludesStatusSaleFieldsAndHistoryTests and MigrationsCreateMissingDatabaseTests rather than duplicating them; MigrationsPreserveExistingRowsTests and ListingMigrationPreservesExistingRowsAndValuesTests are included because the work item names them as coverage that must stay green. Measured at base with the repository pre-commit gate: the two new legacy tests are the only failures (80 of 82 unit tests pass, architecture is 25/25 green, build has 0 warnings, dotnet format --verify-no-changes exits 0), so no collateral red exists and declaredRedTests is empty. A temporary local fix that records only schema-reflected migrations made the full contract command green (7/7) plus all 82 unit and 25 architecture tests, confirming the contract is satisfiable and pins the requested behaviour rather than a mechanism.
